question: Determine the domain and range of $f(x)=\sec^{-1}(x^2-2)$. Clearly indicate all included and excluded endpoint values.
explanation:
Condition for inverse secant
The function $\sec^{-1}u$ is defined when $|u|\geq1$. Therefore, $$|x^2-2|\geq1.$$

Solution of the domain condition
The inequality gives $$x^2-2\leq-1\quad\text{or}\quad x^2-2\geq1.$$ Hence, $x^2\leq1$ or $x^2\geq3$. Therefore, the domain is $$(-\infty,-\sqrt{3}]\cup[-1,1]\cup[\sqrt{3},\infty).$$

Range of the inner expression
On $[-1,1]$, $x^2-2$ takes values in $[-2,-1]$. On the remaining domain intervals, it takes values in $[1,\infty)$.

Corresponding inverse secant values
For arguments in $[1,\infty)$, the range is $\left[0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$. For arguments in $[-2,-1]$, the range is $\left[\frac{2\pi}{3},\pi\right]$.

Final range
Thus, $$\operatorname{Range}(f)=\left[0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\cup\left[\frac{2\pi}{3},\pi\right].$$ The value $\frac{\pi}{2}$ is excluded, while $0$, $\frac{2\pi}{3}$ and $\pi$ are included.
